newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arab Insurance Group takes stake in Moroccan firm.
newsitem.headline: Arab Insurance Group takes stake in Moroccan firm.

text.p: Arab Insurance Group (ARIG) said on Thursday it had acquired the Moroccan government's holdings in Compagnie Nord Africaine et Intercontinentale d'Assurances (CNIA) in cooperation with two Moroccan firms.

ARIG, the Arab world's largest insurance firm, said it had signed an agreement with the Moroccan mutual fund investment company Interfina and insurance company Atlanta last month to purchase 78.5714 percent of CNIA.
"As a result, ARIG now has a 67 percent stake in the company (CNIA)," an ARIG statement said, but gave no details.
General manager of insurance investments Bader Wahidi said: "We are delighted to have had the opportunity to be associated with CNIA and to invest in the large and dynamic Moroccan market."
The statement said Morocco was the largest insurance market in the Arab world with total premiums of around $900 million, of which about 20 percent comes from life insurance.
Bahrain-based ARIG is owned by the governments of Libya, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait. It plans to offer shares worth some $180 million to private investors later this year.
